title: Damage and phase text collide
observed: Hull hit is drawn through PHASE 2 / DANGEROUS SECTOR. Both messages are simultaneously visible after an ordinary accepted collision.
expected: Damage, protection and phase information have separate readable space.
repro: Production /?seed=42, 1280x720; launch and leave controls neutral. At about 24.37s the first hit overlaps the phase label. Also reproduce by natural idle first-hit continuation at 390x844.
cause: .phase-label is absolute at top:100px inside .hud (itself top:30px), while .damage is independently absolute at top:118px. Their horizontal ranges overlap. Portrait uses the same inconsistent coordinate ownership.
subsystem: DOM HUD positioning and notification ownership
solution: Give hull, phase and damage one layout owner and a reserved event row. Damage takes priority; keep phase changes brief. Preserve the peripheral Flight Instrumentation layout.
complexity: S: 0.5–1 implementation day including responsive checks
confidence: High; natural runtime screenshot, video and source agree
human: No for overlap correction; yes for glance readability

title: Phase transition reads like developer telemetry
observed: The three-second phase notice repeats DANGEROUS SECTOR and adds SPEED +8% / RECOVERY GAP -48 without a unit or explanation of recovery gap. Portrait wraps this into multiple lines beside the damage cluster.
expected: A short phase transition tells the player what changes and whether to act.
repro: Reach 500m; inspect 1280x720 or 390x844 during the next three seconds, especially with a first collision.
cause: HUD.update constructs copy directly from RELEASE.phase2SpeedMultiplier, phase1ExtraCells and cellSize; the raw product-facing string lacks a distance unit.
subsystem: Phase UI copy and information hierarchy
solution: Use brief factual copy such as Dangerous sector · Faster flight. Keep exact scheduling parameters in diagnostics; avoid implying a new mechanic. Fold this into UX-01's event row.
complexity: XS: a few hours, dependent on UX-01's layout contract
confidence: High for displayed facts; medium for comprehension impact
human: Yes, check whether new players understand the change

title: Short desktop windows show touch-only steering instructions
observed: At 800x450 with a fine mouse pointer and keyboard, the main menu and flight hint say Drag anywhere to steer / Drag to steer. The CSS chooses touch wording by window shape. Coarse-pointer tablet menus also retain ESC/P and M instructions without touch equivalents.
expected: Control hints reflect the available input method and remain correct when resizing a desktop window.
repro: Open production at 800x450 with isMobile=false, hasTouch=false. Inspect menu and launch. Compare coarse-pointer 768x1024 menu.
state: MENU and PLAYING, fine-pointer small desktop; coarse-pointer tablet
cause: The max-height:520px/min-width:601px rule hides .desktop-control and displays .touch-control unconditionally; max-width:600px does the same. Pointer capability is not the only input into wording.
solution: Select hints by pointer capability or recent input, independently of compact layout. Keep working mouse drag available. Hide keyboard-only auxiliary hints where touch is the only indicated path.
human: No for wording correction; yes for hybrid-device preference

title: Collectible role is absent from first-run guidance
observed: Menu and nine-second flight hint explain steering and avoiding debris. ENERGY appears as 00, but neither surface explains that cyan fragments are optional collections counted for this run. The collector attempt's first success was at 12.56s, after the steering hint had expired.
expected: A new player can distinguish collect from avoid and understand the implemented reward without reading repository documents.
repro: Fresh browser context, launch, inspect the first 15s and results. Compare the menu's Avoid debris. Fly further. with the energy counter and result count.
cause: index.html's mission and hint only describe avoidance. HUD reports a count, with no contextual introduction.
solution: Add one short contextual introduction around the first visible fragment, for example Collect cyan fragments · Optional run count. Explain only current behavior; do not promise fuel, purchases, upgrades or bonus distance. Make repeat-run exposure dismissible or infrequent.
complexity: S–M: 0.5–1.5 days depending on event timing
confidence: High for missing explanation; medium for player effect

title: Existing boundary field has no explicit limit confirmation
observed: The current Combined C fragmented field is already present and responds near edges. At held x=6 the ship stops while the hybrid camera keeps it relatively central; there is no distinct brief limit cue. Sparse field fragments do not form a continuous perimeter.
expected: Players can infer the flight volume and understand a movement clamp without additional playfield clutter.
repro: 1280x720, hold D to the right bound, continue holding, then move to top/left. Compare boundary-right and boundary-right-held states and video.
cause: CONFIG clamps ship center to ±6/±3.6; approved Hybrid follows 80%. ArenaBoundaries already supplies a proximity-brightened fragmented shader, but no explicit clamp-state event is presented.
solution: Validate whether players notice the existing field before adding anything. Compare three small presentation refinements in DESIGN-DIRECTIONS; keep Hybrid, collision bounds and owner-approved Combined C.
complexity: M: 1–3 days for isolated prototypes and comparison, after HUD fixes
confidence: High for existing behavior; medium/low for comprehension impact
human: Yes, essential before choosing a boundary treatment

title: Results do not distinguish a new personal record
observed: The first natural 868m result shows 868m both as distance and personal best with no record acknowledgement or previous-best comparison. The record-broken event reaches a data attribute, but no visible UI consumes it.
expected: A player can immediately recognize an improvement and understand their result.
repro: Use a fresh context, complete a run above zero. Inspect results and compare final distance / personal best; repeat below the saved best.
cause: HUD.feedback sets data-record-broken; CSS and results markup do not show a corresponding acknowledgement. ScoreStorage updates best before results.
solution: Reuse the existing record fact for a compact New personal best label. Retain the large distance and primary replay action. A delta needs a truthful captured previous baseline; avoid fabricated medals or economy.
confidence: High for missing acknowledgement; medium for replay motivation
human: Yes for motivational effect; no for correct record distinction

title: A completed run has no route back to menu or audio settings
observed: Results expose Fly again as the only action. Pause offers resume/restart/sound but no menu. From results, changing volume requires launching another run and pausing it. Browser reload is the available path to the original menu.
expected: A player can finish reviewing a run and choose replay or return to the menu/settings.
repro: Complete any natural run; inspect results buttons and keyboard navigation. Try to return to main menu without reloading.
cause: Results markup has only #replay; Game has no UI transition back to MENU from these states.
solution: Add one subdued Back to menu action on results, with explicit lifecycle cleanup and focus ownership. Consider the same route from pause only if loss of the current run is clearly communicated. Keep replay primary.
complexity: M: 1–2 days; lifecycle work, not just a new link
confidence: High for available actions; medium for frequency/impact

title: Pickup recognition depends on a brief peripheral pulse
observed: Pickup gives a visible local ring, counter increment, +1 and sound. The +1 lasts about 0.42s in the far upper-left cluster, while the pilot attends to the next obstacle. The native collector run verified three accepted pickups; this is a discoverability/glance-risk hypothesis, not a pickup failure.
expected: The existing pickup effect and count are enough to identify a success while avoiding hazards, including muted flight.
repro: Watch native-0-collector at the first pickup (~12.56 gameplay seconds), then the next approach; compare counter and local ring. Repeat muted in a human test.
cause: HUD pulse lifetime follows FEEDBACK.pickup.duration; event association is brief and peripheral. Existing ring and sound are positive redundant cues.
subsystem: Pickup UI feedback, not pickup geometry
solution: First measure recognition with new players. If needed, slightly extend the counter emphasis or add a short nearby text response using the existing event, without beams, extra persistent markers, increased pickup assistance or spawn changes.
complexity: XS–S if validated; a few hours plus muted-play verification
confidence: High that the effect works; low/medium that more persistence is needed
human: Yes; do not implement from screenshots alone

title: Reduced-motion support is not discoverable in game
observed: OS prefers-reduced-motion is respected by renderer and CSS, including reduced streaks/shake and a shorter death sequence. The only settings surface is Audio, with no indication of this existing comfort mode.
expected: A motion-sensitive player can discover how to enable the supported comfort behavior.
repro: Open Sound settings; compare with a context emulating reducedMotion:reduce. Inspect reduced-motion-flight and TESTING facts.
state: MENU/PAUSED settings; PLAYING with OS reduced motion
cause: World reads matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'); settings UI only owns audio.
solution: A small note describing system preference support is the lowest-risk option. Consider an in-game override only if users need it; default to system and reuse the current quality path.
complexity: XS for note; M for persisted system/on/off override
confidence: High for discovery gap; medium for priority
human: Yes, motion-sensitive participants; no clinical comfort claim

title: Audio footer no longer describes the shipped sounds accurately
observed: Audio settings say Original synthesized sounds and ambient music even though accepted collision audio now uses licensed sampled derivatives as well.
expected: User-facing audio copy remains accurate and useful.
repro: Open Audio from menu or pause and read the footer; compare current sample-settings and docs/ASSETS.
cause: Historical index.html footer predates FEEDBACK-001C1 sampled collision audio.
solution: Remove the obsolete production-method sentence or replace it with useful comfort/control guidance. Keep attribution in ASSETS and license notices.
